0.original: <hex:024804F201FC03><hex:024904F201FD03> Quest Sync<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103><hex:02100103>Beott welcomes you to the village of Tomra.

1.original: Beott welcomes you to the village of Tomra with a hearty “lali-ho.” To her dismay, however, it seems that her son, Ronitt, risks becoming a social outcast for his reluctance to maintain the same level of dwarven etiquette. She begs you to befriend the unfriendly boy, hoping that the rarity of a stranger's presence will help draw Ronitt out of his thorny shell...<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Please note that the difficulty of this quest has been synced to your current level.

2.original: Beott introduces you to Ronitt, and the rebellious lad responds to the simplest interactions with snarls and posturing. Following your attempts at a brief “conversation,” it becomes clear that Ronitt has misplaced a family heirloom once belonging to a famous blacksmith. Beott sends the boy off to continue the search, and asks you to question villagers on the hammer's whereabouts.

3.original: You speak with an affable townsdwarf. He commends you on your fine dwarven manners before pointing out another villager who may have picked up the hammer in question.

4.original: You soon learn that the timid townsdwarf did indeed retrieve Ronitt's carelessly misplaced heirloom. Taking charge of the hammer, you set off to return it to its owner.

5.original: You hand the hammer back to Ronitt, who grudgingly admits that you may not be the worst person he's ever met after all. Beott once more urges you to be a friend to her son, before leaving the two of you alone in uncomfortable companionship...

48.original: Well scuff my helm, if it ain't that traveler we've been hearing about! And the elder's had more'n a few things to say!

49.original: Well scuff my helm, if it ain't that foreign dwarf we've been hearing about! Well, well, well, well!

50.original: I'd best be giving you a proper welcome then, eh?<hex:02100103>Lali-ho!

54.original: Now that's what I like to see─a “lali-ho” straight from the heart!

55.original: ...To be expected, I suppose─outsiders can't never get the greeting right the first time! Never mind, never mind!

56.original: I only wish my own boy would put a bit more effort into his “lalis” and his “hos.” He's always busy fiddling with his damn automata; no time for swapping words with folk of flesh and blood.

57.original: Every dwarf knows that a “lali-ho” gets a “lali-ho,” or you're asking to become an outcast... A mother does worry, she does.

58.original: And that's only the half of it! I know it's just a stage all lads go through, but the little bugger has to argue with every word I say!

59.original: ...Oh, I've just had the most clever idea!

60.original: He'll not listen to me or the other villagers, but maybe─just maybe─curiosity for a stranger will win out over that sour attitude of his. Worth a try, don't you think?

61.original: Please, befriend my son, Ronitt. Just...get him used to giving a proper greeting. That's all I ask.

62.original: And I tell you, he really is a marvel with automata! If you end up getting along, he might even show you a few of his stranger contraptions!

63.original: Roooniiitt! Look, we've got a visitor! Why don't you say hello?

65.original: What!? You got somethin' to say to me!?

71.original: Huh? Th-That's not how we... Hmph.

72.original: What kinda greeting is that!? A-Are you tryin' to impress me, or somethin'? I... Hmph.

74.original: Oh, Ronitt, my lad, you can do better than that! Head up, eyes front! No need to be shy!

76.original: Yes, dear, if you say so. Now, Ronitt, is everything else alright? You seemed to be looking for something...?

77.original: Oh, no, it's just... I mean, I sorta...lost my hammer.

78.original: You WHAT!? Of all the irresponsible, careless, foolish...

79.original: Ronitt's hammer has been in the family for generations! It's a priceless heirloom that once belonged to Watts, the blacksmith of legend himself!

80.original: Well, what're you standing around for, boy! Find that hammer! <hex:021A020203>We<hex:021A020103> will do what we can to help.

81.original: Right, why don't you have a chat with some villagers for me and ask if they've seen Ronitt's hammer. Just remember your dwarven manners, and all will be well!

82.original: Odd, I swear I was just holdin' it...

83.original: Hm? What're you starin' at, eh!? Clear off!

84.original: You want words with me, then?

88.original: Oho! That's a fine “lali-ho” you've got there, <hex:02080EE905FF056C617373FF046C616403>. I like you!

89.original: ...Hm? <hex:020810E905FF065368652773FF054865277303> trying to tell me something, I just know it...

90.original: Ronitt...? Ah, that sulky sprout's lost old Watts's hammer, has he? Well lucky for him, I believe yon gentledwarf picked it up!

91.original: It's time I was getting back to work, then. Good day to you, stranger!

96.original: Wh-What's this!? A perfect “lali-ho”!? Y-You're no ordinary traveler, I see!

97.original: Argh! Wh-Why is <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503> showing me the top of <hex:02080DE905FF04686572FF0468697303> h-head!? Has <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503> no <hex:021A020203>shame<hex:021A020103>!?

98.original: ...The h-hammer I picked up? Aye, I reckoned I would hand it over to the elder for safekeeping. Y-You're saying it belongs to young R-Ronitt?

99.original: Well, h-he can be a touch sh-shouty, that boy... D-Do you think you could take it back to him for m-me?

101.original: Huh? Why are you still here!?

103.original: Well, well, well, well. Would you look at that!

104.original: You see, Ronitt? Give the right and proper greeting, and folk'll be glad to share a bit of kindness. Could be that you've a thing or two to learn from <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203> here.

106.original: Aye, well, maybe... Maybe you're not such a bad sort.

107.original: I'll just put the hammer in a safe place somewhere... I mean to be a famous smitty myself someday, so I'd best not lose it again!

108.original: I'll leave you to it, then. I know my boy's not the easiest to get along with, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, but he could sure use a friend like you!

109.original: I don't need a friend! I don't need anyone!

110.original: We...we're not goin' to be friends, understand!? But you can stay around a little longer. If you want.

112.original: Well, now, what's that you've got there?
